The SEI module for the MY component

Source: R/adult-MY-SEI.R
SEI.Rd

Implements the MY component using a Susceptible-Exposed-Infectious (SEI) compartmental model of adult mosquito infection dynamics. Mosquito abundance, exposed mosquitoes, and infectious mosquitoes are tracked separately across patches.

State Variables

M

density of adult mosquitoes

Y

density of infected (exposed) adult mosquitoes

Z

density of infectious adult mosquitoes

Dynamical Terms

Lambda or \(\Lambda\)

adult mosquito emergence rate, computed by ramp.xds::Emergence

kappa or \(\kappa\)

net infectiousness, computed by ramp.xds::Transmission

Parameters

f

blood feeding rate — use ramp.xds::setup_f or ramp.xds::setup_blood_feeding_rates

q

human fraction — use ramp.xds::setup_q or ramp.xds::setup_human_fractions

g

mosquito mortality rate — use ramp.xds::setup_g or ramp.xds::setup_mosquito_mortality

sigma or \(\sigma\)

emigration rate — use ramp.xds::setup_sigma or ramp.xds::setup_mosy_emigration

mu or \(\mu\)

fraction of emigrating mosquitoes lost — use ramp.xds::setup_mu or ramp.xds::setup_emigration_loss

K or K_matrix

mosquito dispersal matrix — use ramp.xds::setup_K_matrix

eip or \(\tau\)

extrinsic incubation period — use ramp.xds::setup_eip

nu or \(\nu\)

oviposition rate: the number of egg batches laid in each patch, per mosquito, per day — use ramp.xds::setup_nu or ramp.xds::setup_egg_batch_rates

eggsPerBatch or \(\Gamma\)

number of eggs per batch

After basic setup, change_MY_pars.SEI can be used to change parameter values. Bionomic parameters are configured as static baselines by default.

Survival and Dispersal

Mosquito survival and dispersal are described by the demographic matrix \(\Omega\). The parameter \(g\) is the per-capita mortality rate while mosquitoes are in a patch. Mosquitoes emigrate from patches at per-capita rates \(\sigma\), and a fraction \(\mu\) of emigrating mosquitoes is lost. The total rate of loss from a patch is $$g+\mu\sigma.$$ The columns of the dispersal matrix \(K\) sum to zero. For non-trivial dispersal matrices, \(\mbox{diag}(K)=-1\); its off-diagonal elements describe the fractions of surviving emigrants that arrive in other patches. The demographic matrix is $$\Omega=\mbox{diag}(g+\sigma\mu)-K\cdot\mbox{diag}(\sigma(1-\mu)).$$

Blood Feeding

The blood feeding rate \(f\) and human fraction \(q\) determine the rate of human blood feeding, \(fq\). Natural constraints are \(f=0\) when no blood hosts are available, \(q=0\) when no humans are available, and \(q=1\) when humans are the only available hosts.

Dynamics

Adult mosquitoes emerge from aquatic habitats at rate \(\Lambda\). Mosquitoes become exposed when they take an infectious human blood meal; exposed mosquitoes progress to the infectious class at rate \(1/\tau\), where \(\tau\) is the EIP. The model equations are $$ \begin{array}{rl} dM/dt &= \Lambda-\Omega\cdot M \\\\ dY/dt &= fq\kappa(M-Y)-\Omega\cdot Y \\\\ dZ/dt &= (Y-Z)/\tau-\Omega\cdot Z \end{array} $$

DTS

Update_MYt.SEI updates M and Z using the stored Omega directly. The updating equations use D = xds_obj$MYday and the module field ccc. The method returns these two updated states as a list; it does not update Y.

Infective Biting

The patch-level human biting density, fqM, is \(f q M\); the infective biting density, fqZ, is \(f q Z\). F_fqM.SEI and F_fqZ.SEI compute these quantities from the total and infectious mosquito densities, respectively. ramp.xds::compute_EIR combines fqZ with the biting distribution matrix and resident-bite fraction to compute stratum-level EIR; ramp.xds::F_hbr uses fqM to compute stratum-level HBR.

Egg Laying

The oviposition rate \(\nu\) and the number of eggs per batch \(\Gamma\) determine the egg production rate per patch: $$G=\nu\Gamma M.$$ F_eggs.SEI computes \(G\), which is passed to ramp.xds::EggLaying for distribution among aquatic habitats.
